spots.name: Milan Cathedral
spots.summary: Milan Cathedral, or Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica of the Nativity of Saint Mary, is the cathedral church of Milan, Lombardy, Italy. Dedicated to the Nativity of St. Mary, it is the seat of the Archbishop of Milan, currently Archbishop Mario Delpini.

names.ja: ミラノのドゥオーモ

spots.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
spots.summary: The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II is Italy's oldest active shopping arcade and a major landmark of Milan. Housed within a four-story double arcade in the centre of town, the Galleria is named after Victor Emmanuel II, the first king of the Kingdom of Italy.

names.ja: ヴィットーリオ・エマヌエーレ2世のガッレリア

spots.name: San Siro
spots.summary: The Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, commonly known as the San Siro, is a football stadium in the San Siro district of Milan, Italy. Nicknamed "La Scala del calcio", it has a seating capacity of 75,817, making it the largest stadium in Italy and one of the largest stadiums in Europe.

names.ja: スタディオ・ジュゼッペ・メアッツァ

spots.name: Sforza Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sforza Castle is a medieval fortification located in Milan, northern Italy. It was built in the 15th century by Francesco Sforza, Duke of Milan, on the remnants of a 14th-century fortification. Later renovated and enlarged, in the 16th and 17th centuries it was one of the largest citadels in Europe.

names.ja: スフォルツェスコ城

spots.name: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Cimitero Monumentale is one of the two largest cemeteries in Milan, Italy, the other one being the Cimitero Maggiore. It is noted for the abundance of artistic tombs and monuments.

names.ja: ミラノ記念墓地

spots.name: piazza del Duomo
spots.summary: Piazza del Duomo is the main piazza of Milan, Italy. It is named after, and dominated by, Milan Cathedral. The piazza marks the center of the city, both in a geographic sense and because of its importance from an artistic, cultural, and social point of view.

names.ja: 大聖堂広場

spots.name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
spots.summary: Santa Maria delle Grazie is a church and Dominican convent in Milan, northern Italy, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The convent contains the mural of The Last Supper by Leonardo da Vinci, which is in the refectory.

names.fr: Église Santa Maria delle Grazie de Milan
names.it: Chiesa di Santa Maria delle Grazie
names.ja: サンタ・マリア・デッレ・グラツィエ教会

spots.name: La Scala
spots.summary: La Scala is a historic opera house in Milan, Italy. The theatre was inaugurated on 3 August 1778 and was originally known as il Nuovo Regio Ducale Teatro alla Scala. The premiere performance was Antonio Salieri's Europa riconosciuta.

names.ja: スカラ座

spots.name: Rondanini Pietà

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Rondanini Pietà is a marble sculpture that Michelangelo worked on from 1552 until the last days of his life, in 1564. Several sources indicate that there were actually three versions, with this one being the last.

names.ja: ロンダニーニのピエタ

spots.name: Milano Centrale railway station
spots.summary: Milano Centrale is the main railway station of the city of Milan, Northern Italy, and is the second busiest railway station in Italy for passenger flow and the largest railway station in Europe by volume.

names.ja: ミラノ中央駅

spots.name: Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio
spots.summary: The Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio, officially known as Basilica romana minore collegiata abbaziale prepositurale di Sant'Ambrogio, is an ancient Romanesque-style, Roman Catholic church located in the center of Milan, in the region of Lombardy, Italy.

names.ja: サンタンブロージョ教会

spots.name: Royal Palace of Milan

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Royal Palace of Milan was the seat of government in the Italian city of Milan for many centuries. Today, it serves as a cultural centre and it is home to international art exhibitions.

names.ja: ミラノ王宮

spots.name: Madonnina
spots.summary: The Madonnina is a statue of the Virgin Mary atop Milan Cathedral in Italy. The Madonnina is the subject of the most traditional Milanese song, O mia bella Madonnina. The Derby della Madonnina named after it is the local rivalry between the city's two football clubs A.C. Milan and Inter Milan.

spots.name: Pinacoteca di Brera

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Pinacoteca di Brera is the main public gallery for paintings in Milan, Italy. It contains one of the foremost collections of Italian paintings from the 13th to the 20th century, an outgrowth of the cultural program of the Brera Academy, which shares the site in the Palazzo Brera.

names.ja: ブレラ美術館

spots.name: Bosco Verticale
spots.summary: The Bosco Verticale is a complex of two residential skyscrapers designed by Boeri Studio and located in the Porta Nuova district of Milan, Italy. They have a height of 116 metres (381 ft) and 84 m (276 ft) and within the complex is an 11-story office building.

names.ja: ボスコ・ヴェルティカーレ

spots.name: Museo del Novecento

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museo del Novecento is a museum of twentieth-century art in Milan, in Lombardy in northern Italy. It is housed in the Palazzo dell'Arengario, near Piazza del Duomo in the centre of the city.

names.ja: 20世紀美術館

spots.name: San Bernardino alle Ossa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Bernardino alle Ossa is a church in Milan, northern Italy, best known for its ossuary, a small side chapel decorated with numerous human skulls and bones.

names.it: Chiesa di San Bernardino alle Ossa

spots.name: Parco Sempione
spots.summary: Sempione Park is a green area in the city of Milan. Built at the end of the 19th century on the area previously occupied by the Piazza d'armi, it covers an area of 386,000 m2 (4,150,000 sq ft), completely fenced and under video surveillance.

spots.name: Arch of Peace
spots.summary: The triumphal arch of peace stands at the place at one of Milan's seven city gates. First the gate was known as Porta Giovia and was closer to the city center. Porta Sempione means "Gate towards Simplon", and once the road leading over the Simplon Pass to Paris went through this gate. The current gate was built in the early 19th century and at that time it was referred to as Arco della Pace.

names.ja: 平和の門

spots.name: Piazzale Loreto
spots.summary: Piazzale Loreto is a major city square in Milan, Italy.

names.ja: ロレート広場

spots.name: Palazzo dell'Arengario

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo dell'Arengario is an early-20th century complex of two symmetrical buildings in Piazza del Duomo, the central piazza of Milan, Italy. It was completed in the 1950s and currently houses the Museo del Novecento, a museum dedicated to 20th-century art.

spots.name: Triennale di Milano

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Triennale di Milano is a museum of art and design in the Parco Sempione in Milan, in Lombardy in northern Italy. It is housed in the Palazzo dell'Arte, built between 1931 and 1933 to designs by Giovanni Muzio and financed by Antonio Bernocchi and his brothers Andrea and Michele.

names.ja: ミラノ・トリエンナーレ

spots.name: Santa Maria presso San Satiro

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Santa Maria presso San Satiro is a church in Milan. The Italian Renaissance structure (1476–1482) houses the early medieval shrine to Satyrus, brother of Saint Ambrose. The church is known for its false apse, an early example of trompe-l'œil, attributed to Donato Bramante.

names.fr: Église Santa Maria presso San Satiro
names.es: Iglesia de Santa Maria presso San Satiro
names.it: Chiesa di Santa Maria presso San Satiro

spots.name: Santa Tecla, Milan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Basilica di Santa Tecla was a former, paleo-Christian basilica church in Milan, region of Lombardy, Italy. It was originally established in 350 and demolished in 1458. Remnants of the structure have been excavated underneath the Milan Cathedral.

spots.name: Pirelli Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Pirelli Tower is a 32-storey, 127 m (417 ft) skyscraper in Milan, Italy. The base of the building is 1,900 m2 (20,000 sq ft), with a length of 75.5 m (248 ft) and a width of 20.5 m (67 ft). The construction used approximately 30,000 m3 (1,100,000 cu ft) of concrete.

names.ja: ピレリ・ビル

spots.name: Palazzo Marino

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Palazzo Marino is a 16th-century palace located in Piazza della Scala, in the centre of Milan, Italy. It has been Milan's city hall since 9 September 1861. It borders on Piazza San Fedele, Piazza della Scala, Via Case Rotte and Via Tommaso Marino.

spots.name: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore is a church in Milan, Northern Italy. It was originally attached to the most important female convent of the Benedictines in the city, Monastero Maggiore, which is now in use as the Civic Archaeological Museum.

names.fr: Église San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
names.es: Iglesia de San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore
names.it: Chiesa di San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore

spots.name: Torre Velasca

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Torre Velasca is a skyscraper built in the 1950s by the BBPR architectural partnership, in Milan, Italy. The construction was achieved in 1958, and inaugurated in 1961. Measuring 106 metres in height to the roof, the tower has 26 stories.

spots.name: Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Milano

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Milano is a museum in Milan, Italy dedicated to the study of animals, plants, and the natural environment, including geology. Exhibits include dinosaurs and Italy's largest collection of dioramas of ecosystems.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Milano

names.fr: Museo Civico di Storia Naturale de Milan
names.es: Museo Cívico de Historia Natural de Milán
names.ja: ミラノ市立自然史博物館

spots.name: monument to Victor Emmanuel II
spots.summary: An equestrian statue of Victor Emmanuel II is installed in Milan, Italy.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Equestrian statue of Victor Emmanuel II, Milan

spots.name: Piazza della Scala
spots.summary: Piazza della Scala is a pedestrian central square of Milan, Italy. It is connected to the main square of Milan, Piazza del Duomo, by the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II passage.

names.ja: スカーラ広場

spots.name: Palazzo della Ragione

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo della Ragione is a historic building in Milan, Italy, located in Piazza Mercanti, facing the Loggia degli Osii. Built in the 13th century, it originally served as a broletto—an administrative and judicial building. As the second broletto constructed in Milan, it is also known as the Broletto Nuovo.

spots.name: Piazza Mercanti
spots.summary: Piazza Mercanti is a central city square of Milan, Italy. It is located between Piazza del Duomo, which marks the centre of the modern city of Milan, and Piazza Cordusio, and it used to be the heart of the city in the Middle Ages.

spots.name: Chiaravalle Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abbey of Santa Maria di Rovegnano is a Cistercian monastic complex in the comune of Milan, Lombardy, northern Italy. The borgo that has developed round the abbey was once an independent commune called Chiaravalle Milanese, now included in Milan and referred to as the Chiaravalle district.

photo.author: The original uploader was Yoruno at Italian Wikipedia.

spots.name: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci in Milan, dedicated to painter and scientist Leonardo da Vinci, is the largest science and technology museum in Italy. It was opened on 15 February 1953 and inaugurated by Prime Minister Alcide De Gasperi.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museo Nazionale Scienza e Tecnologia Leonardo da Vinci

spots.name: Basilica of San Lorenzo
spots.summary: The Basilica of San Lorenzo Maggiore is a Roman Catholic church in Milan, Northern Italy. Located within the city's ring of navigli, it is one of the oldest churches in the city, originally built in Roman times, but subsequently rebuilt several times over the centuries.

names.ja: サン・ロレンツォ大聖堂

spots.name: UniCredit Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The UniCredit Tower is an office skyscraper in Milan, Italy. The building's spire increases its height to 238 metres (781 ft), making it the tallest building in Italy, although the Allianz Tower, at 210 m (690 ft), ranks the tallest by roof height.

names.ja: ウニクレディト・タワー

spots.name: Idroscalo
spots.summary: The Idroscalo is an artificial lake in Milan, Italy that was originally constructed as a seaplane airport. It opened on 28 October 1930, in the heyday of seaplanes. When the use of seaplanes for passenger transport declined it became a recreational and sport facility.

spots.name: Torre Branca
spots.summary: Torre Branca is a steel-frame panoramic tower designed by architect Giò Ponti in 1933, located in Parco Sempione, the main city park of Milan, Italy. The top of the tower is a panoramic point whose view, on a clear day, may encompass the Milan cityline as well as the Alps, the Apennines, and part of the Po Valley.

spots.name: Via Monte Napoleone
spots.summary: Via Monte Napoleone, also spelled Via Montenapoleone, is an upscale shopping street in Milan, Italy, and the most expensive street in the world (2024).

names.ja: モンテナポレオーネ通り

spots.name: Museo Poldi Pezzoli

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Museo Poldi Pezzoli is an art museum in Milan, Italy. It is located near the Teatro alla Scala, on Via Manzoni 12.

names.ja: ボルディ・ペッツォーリ美術館

spots.name: San Fedele, Milan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: San Fedele is a Jesuit church in Milan, northern Italy. It is dedicated to St. Fidelis of Como, patron of the Catholic diocese of Como. Presently it remains a parish church, owned by the Jesuit order, though focusing on religious works.

names.ja: サン・フェデーレ教会

hours.note: Closed Mon

names.ja: アンブロシアーナ絵画館

spots.name: Basilica di Santo Stefano Maggiore

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Basilica di Santo Stefano Maggiore is a church in Milan, Italy. It was established in the 5th century. Originally dedicated to both Saint Zechariah and Saint Stephen, it was later dedicated to Saint Stephen only. Throughout its history, has undergone several reconstructions, expansion and restoration.

spots.name: Pinacoteca del Castello Sforzesco

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Pinacoteca del Castello Sforzesco is an art gallery in the museum complex of the Sforza Castle in Milan, Italy.

names.ja: スフォルツェスコ城 絵画館

spots.name: Mediolanum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mediolanum, the ancient city where Milan now stands, was originally an Insubrian city, but afterwards became an important Roman city in Northern Italy.

names.ja: ミラノ

spots.name: Royal Villa of Milan

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Villa Belgiojoso Bonaparte, also known as Villa Reale and formerly called Villa Comunale, is a palace in Milan, in Lombardy in northern Italy. It was built between 1790 and 1796 as the residence of Count Ludovico Barbiano di Belgiojoso. The villa is in Neoclassical style, and was designed by Leopoldo Pollack.

spots.name: Porta Sempione
spots.summary: Porta Sempione is a city gate of Milan, Italy. The name is used both to refer to the gate proper and to the surrounding district (quartiere), a part of the Zone 1 division, including the major avenue of Corso Sempione.

spots.name: University of Milan, Ca' Granda headquarters

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Renaissance complex which now serves the university.

spots.name: Palazzo Belgioioso

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Belgioioso is a palatial residence in the northern Italian city of Milan, completed in 1781 in a Neoclassical style by Giuseppe Piermarini.

spots.name: San Gottardo, Milan

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: San Gottardo in Corte or San Gottardo a Palazzo is a church in Milan, northern Italy.

names.it: Chiesa di San Gottardo in Corte

spots.name: San Nazaro in Brolo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The basilica of San Nazaro in Brolo or San Nazaro Maggiore is a 4th-century Roman Catholic church located in Piazza San Nazzaro in Brolo in Milan, region of Lombardy, Italy.

spots.name: Galleria d'Arte Moderna, Milan

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Galleria d'Arte Moderna is a modern art museum in Milan, in Lombardy in northern Italy. It is housed in the Villa Reale, at Via Palestro 16, opposite the Giardini Pubblici Indro Montanelli. The collection consists largely of Italian and European works from the eighteenth to the twentieth centuries.

names.ja: ミラノ市立近代美術館

spots.name: Archaeological Museum, Milan

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Archaeological Museum of Milan is located in the ex-convent of the Monastero Maggiore, alongside the ancient church of San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore, with entrance on Corso Magenta.

names.ja: ミラノ考古学博物館

spots.name: Casa degli Omenoni

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Casa degli Omenoni is a historic palace of Milan, northern Italy, located in the eponymous street of Via degli Omenoni. It was designed by sculptor Leone Leoni for himself; he both lived and worked there.

spots.name: Ca' de Sass

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ca' de Sass is a monumental 19th century building in Milan, Italy. Located in the city centre, at 6 and 8 of Via Monte di Pietà, is the headquarters of Intesa Sanpaolo, the largest Italian banking group.

spots.name: Basilica of Sant'Eustorgio

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of Sant'Eustorgio is a church in Milan in northern Italy, which is in the Basilicas Park city park. It was for many years an important stop for pilgrims on their journey to Rome or to the Holy Land, because it was said to contain the tomb of the Three Magi or Three Kings.

names.ja: サンテウストルジョ聖堂

spots.name: Palazzo Litta

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palazzo Litta, also known as the Palazzo Arese-Litta, is a Baroque structure in Milan, northern Italy, opposite San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore, and dating from the period of Spanish rule of the city. In 2018, it served as a cultural center, housing exhibition spaces, offices, and a theater.

spots.name: Generali Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Generali Tower, or Hadid Tower, is an office skyscraper completed in 2017 in Milan, Italy that reaches a height of 177.4 m (582 ft) with 44 floors, and a total floor area of about 67,000 square metres (720,000 sq ft). Its designer is the Anglo-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid, hence it is also called torre Hadid.

names.ja: ゼネラリタワー

spots.name: Gallerie di Piazza Scala

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Gallerie d'Italia - Milano is a modern and contemporary museum in Milan, Italy.

names.ja: ガレリエ・ディ・ピアッツァ・スカーラ

spots.name: Corso Vittorio Emanuele II
spots.summary: One of the most popular high street shopping arteries in the city. It has a very elegant modern appearance, but too has some well-preserved grand 18th- and 19th-century buildings, including a rotunda-like neoclassical church. The Corso contains some great retail stores, including big shopping centres, fashionable outlets, and youthful, sporty designer boutiques. It is pedestrian.

names.ja: ヴィットーリオ・エマヌエーレ2世通り
names.zh: 维托里奥·埃马努埃莱大街

spots.name: Expo Gate
spots.summary: Information hub and ticket office for the Expo Milano 2015. The gate consists of two structures designed by Scandurra Studio.

spots.name: Corso Magenta
spots.summary: An elegant and aristocratic street in the north-western part of Milan. It contains sophisticated cafes and shops, and also some fine, mainly Baroque, palaces, notably the Palazzo Litta, one of the best examples of 18th century Milanese architecture, and also a place in which Napoleon I spent some time. Metro stations Conciliazione, Cadorna, Cairoli and Cordusio are the closest to the avenue. The f

spots.name: Piazza Duca d'Aosta
spots.summary: A very big, relatively modern and busy square in the north-east of Milan, famous for hosting the city's majestic central station, and the Pirelli skyscraper. The Piazza is generally bustling with people, and is at the heart of Milan's economic and business district. It is where you'll end up if you need to go to the central station, but it is also a good place to go because it boasts some excellen

spots.name: Boschi Di Stefano House Museum
spots.summary: Extensive collection of 20th century art. Building (1929–1931) and some furniture by Piero Portaluppi.

spots.name: Museo San Siro Collezione Milan Inter

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Inter and Milan paraphernalia are at display at the museum in the stadium that two of the most famous football (soccer) teams in Italy call home.

spots.name: Piazza del Liberty

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small square, which however, is noted for a stunning Art Nouveau palace today called the Hotel del Corso, but once the Trianon. You reach it just off a tiny opening at the beginning of the Corso Vittorio Emanuele.

spots.name: Piazzale Cadorna
spots.summary: Medium-sized, normal square in central Milan with the funky modern North Station and some fine buildings, but notably a set of peculiar modern sculptures in the middle.

spots.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria delle Grazie al Naviglio
spots.summary: This landmark at the northern bank of Naviglio Grande bears the same name as the UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Western part of the country. The church is just a little over a century old, built in Romanesque Revival style, and is the third church built on that place.

spots.name: Gardens of the Guastalla
spots.summary: Among Milan's oldest (founded in the 16th century), but quite small gardens, and are very close to the University district. The parks, however, were only opened to the public in the early 20th century. You can have a nice walk inside, and you also have a classical temple-like structure and also a sort of pond with a Baroque railing surrounding it. Reachable via Crocetta, P.ta Romana, Missori or ev

spots.name: Armani/Nobu
spots.summary: Part of Japanese restaurant chain serving sushi with South American influences in Armani-themed surroundings. Apart from sushi, dishes such as ceviche, spicy tuna, different soups, lobster, seaweed, salmon, or different forms of vegetables and meat (and several others) are on the menu, and you can find desserts such as carrot cakes, tea ice creams, chocolates, exotic fruits, or different, both Eur

spots.name: Just Cavalli
spots.summary: Found inside the Torre Branca in the big, leafy Sempione park, the Just Cavalli Hollywood was the brainchild of Roberto Cavalli, the fashion designer. It was renovated in 2009-10. For beginners, one can find cheese, tuna tartar, Parma ham, and caviar, and for the main course, you can eat dishes of spaghetti, risotto, small gnocchi with crab, different forms of seafood, veal, steak, and different f

spots.name: Biffi
spots.summary: Opened in 1867, it is an old fashioned restaurant/café in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, surrounded by a plethora of interesting shops, which serves drinks, and foods such as spaghetti, veal, steak, fish, and desserts such as chocolate Sacher, Tiramisu, ice cream and fruit salads. The waiters serve in the formal white gloves.

spots.name: Savini

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Opened in 1867, the Savini is a fancy and well-established restaurant inside the magnificent Galleria, serving meals such as Milanese-style risotto, spaghetti and ravioli, meat cutlet, lamb and beef, different forms of fish, warmly-made Tirmisu, and other forms of desserts including chocolate cake and tart with strawberries.

spots.name: El Brellin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For a classic take on Milanese cooking, try Ill Brellin, where you can choose from homey classics such as rigatoni sautéed with pancetta, to modern interpretations on typical ingredients—a pumpkin tart as an appetizer. Outdoor seating makes this a perfect choice on a sunny day, although it is closed for dinner on Sundays.

spots.name: La Terrazza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For a Mediterranean take on Japanese cuisine, head to La Terraza which serves fusion food among a contemporary decor. During the summer months, everyone heads to the terrace, where you can see the treetops of the nearby Giardini Pubblici. There's a "happy hour" every day except Sunday; on Sunday, brunch is served.

spots.name: Bar Magenta

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This popular bar is best visited with a bunch of friends during apperitivo, a time when free appetizers are given out, usually around 19:00. It was said that Bar Magenta coined the now very popular “aperitivo”, and having a drink in here is a classic experience.

spots.name: Rita

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: It is the perfect place for a cocktail and Edo, the barman and the owner together with the chief Luca, is the grandmaster. They have strict code for preparing cocktails: no syrups are admitted, only fresh fruit. It is also a perfect place to eat.

spots.name: Tram restaurant ATMosfera

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: ATM, which operates the public transport in Milan, has created a tram restaurant. A tram of the class "Carrello" from 1928 has been transformed into a restaurant on tracks and you can have dinner and see many of Milan's sights at the same time.

spots.name: Pianeta Luna

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A self service restaurant near the Central Railway Station, with pizza, pasta and other classic Italian dishes and English speaking staff. Very reasonable prices and good food combined with a wide variety of wines - this is not a tourist trap.

spots.name: Osteria del Gnocco Fritto

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: At Osteria del Gnocco Fritto the €4.50 cover charge includes baskets of fried hand-size pastries (similar to sopapillas) accompanied by meats, cheeses, or jams (€8 to €11). The restaurant has a second location closer to the city center.

spots.name: Caffè Cova

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in 1817, this pasticceria (pastry shop) relocated to the exclusive Montenapoleone street in 1950, and is a good place for a cake/tart with a hot drink, such as coffee. At Christmas, enjoy the traditional Panettone cake.

spots.name: Emporio Armani Caffè

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Found on the ground floor of the Armani Megastore, this café is all Armani themed. It's a good place to stop for a drink after a day of shopping, since it is really close to the ritzy Via Manzoni and Via Monte Napoleone.

spots.name: Pizzeria Gino Sorbillo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Probably the best pizza in town at a reasonable price. The restaurant reopens for dinner at 19:00, people will be lining up in front of the entrance beforehand (because the pizza is so good). Come early to avoid waiting!

spots.name: Honky Tonks

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Not exactly a country cowboy bar as the name might imply, a more accurate description would include the smoky lounge feel and the jazz music being played. The drinks are well made and they also serve Tex-Mex style food.

spots.name: Dolce e Gabbana Martini Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Dolce & Gabbana themed bar, it is in the posh Venezia avenue, right in the top fashion district. Good place to enjoy a Martini cocktail in Dolce & Gabbana surroundings after some shopping or sightseeing.

spots.name: Roialto

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Its bland façade conceals a real gem of a cocktail bar/restaurant. It is a very popular spot for after-work drinks, or perhaps a pre-club drink if you're going dancing somewhere like the Gattopardo.

spots.name: Pizzeria Da Giuliano

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nice and cozy pizzeria with great, quite thick and large pizza slices. You can choose your toppings and after a few minutes you'll get your slice. Wood burning oven and loads of Mozzarella.

spots.name: Bar Bianco

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: It's cash only at this bar, but with Gucci-clad clubbers and their well-suited companions, money seems easy to come by. The life of a party can always be detected in here.

spots.name: La Ravioleria Sarpi
spots.summary: Maybe the best place to have Chinese dumplings in Italy. Many selections available (pork, beef or vegetarian). They also sell a Chinese version of crêpes. Only takeaway.

spots.name: Viale Bligny
spots.summary: Street in Milan
